sources: Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, in interview with Al Mayadeen TV (excerpts released Wed Nov 11)
fault_line: Keep the 60% uranium as untouchable national wealth -- or trade it away to lift the blockade and sanctions? Which price is worth paying?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the rejection] Rezaei said Iran will not allow 'even a single particle' of enriched nuclear material to leave the country, rejecting a US proposal to transfer its stockpile of 60%-enriched uranium to a third country; Russia, which offered to receive and store the uranium, has been informed of Tehran's decision. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the retaliation warning] 'Any new US attacks will also be met with targeting US bases far away,' he told Al Mayadeen. [VERIFIED FACT -- no talks] Rezaei said there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran and Washington. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the rationale] 'We need the enriched material to design ships and submarines that work on nuclear energy,' Rezaei said; Tehran will use it itself. [CONTEXT -- the opening left] While Iran has repeatedly rejected transfer abroad, it has NOT ruled out diluting the uranium to a lower enrichment level under international supervision. [CONTEXT -- the stockpile] The IAEA estimated Iran held 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60% before Israel and the US attacked three Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025; how much survived is unclear. Iran has sent the US a nuclear proposal via Qatar, to be discussed only after Washington meets Tehran's seven demands.
sections.what_verified: 4 distinct tiered publisher families carry the same on-record statement: Reuters (T1), Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA), Times of Israel (T3), Daily Sabah (T3). ZeroHedge, Republic World and Times Live carry the same wire but have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count.
sections.what_disputed: The position itself is a restatement: Rezaei said the same on Oct 20 (to Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir), and FM spokesman Baghaei rejected the transfer on Nov 2 and Nov 9. What is NEW on Nov 11: the Wednesday Al Mayadeen interview, the explicit 'Russia has been informed' detail, the retaliation warning against US bases, and the ships/submarines rationale. The US has not publicly replied to the seven conditions; no IAEA verification of the current stockpile exists since the June 2025 strikes. The 440.9 kg figure is a pre-strike estimate, not a current inventory.
sections.why_matters: Iran's nuclear red line, on camera: 'not a single particle leaves' -- and Moscow already knows.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (AJ liveblog updated 13:52Z = 17:52 ; Reuters wire; Times Live 13:35:48Z = 17:35 ) -- Iran's security chief Rezaei: not 'a single particle' of enriched uranium leaves Iran; Russia informed; fresh US strikes would draw retaliation on US bases

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran's nuclear red line, on camera: 'not a single particle leaves' -- and Moscow already knows. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Keep the 60% uranium as untouchable national wealth -- or trade it away to lift the blockade and sanctions? Which price is worth paying?
